statements.t: The amount of the provision for (release of) credit losses is derived from the Company’s quarterly Current Expected Credit Loss (“CECL”) model.
For loans that are individually evaluated, the Company uses two impairment measurement methods: 1) the present value of expected future cash flows and 2) collateral value.

The Company performs periodic and systematic detailed reviews of its loan portfolio to determine management’s estimate of the lifetime expected credit losses.

Martin Resch, the Company’s President and Chief Executive Officer, noted, “We are pleased with our third quarter financial results, reflecting continued profitability growth throughout all of our lines of business.” Resch added, “Recent CassPay and Facilities client wins, combined with higher transportation and facility dollar volumes, present us with an enviable outlook for continued growth in assets, net…

The improved revenue outlook, when combined with additional technology enhancements designed to improve client experience and reinforce our competitive advantages, should allow for enhanced profitability for the next several quarters.”

While the Company believes it will continue to achieve operational efficiencies in certain areas due to technology successes, this progress may be offset short-term as a result of anticipated investments in people and resources needed to get other AI-enabled systems in place and operating at a level where the Company can continue to achieve operational efficiencies in future periods.
